Who among these is a physicist?
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Ingrid Daubechies is a mathematician. Baroness Ingrid Daubechies ( doh-bə-SHEE; French: [dobʃi]; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
What is the atomic number of Copernicium?
Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
What is the atomic number of Thallium?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
In what year did Johann Wolfgang von Goethe die?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year was Nitrogen discovered?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Which company manufactures Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: Skunk Works. It was the first operational aircraft to be designed with stealth technology.
Which country is Panavia Tornado from?
Panavia Tornado: Italy. It first flew on 14 August 1974 and was introduced into service in 1979–1980.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.
A pioneer of industrial toxicology, this American physician trained at Michigan, worked out of Hull House in Chicago, and led the fight to curb lead poisoning in the workplace — who was she?
Alice Hamilton (February 27, 1869 - September 22, 1970) was an American physician, research scientist, and author.
Nicknamed the 'nail mosquito,' this genus — first classified in 1818 — is the sole mosquito genus known to carry human malaria — which genus is it?
Anopheles is a genus of mosquito first described by the German entomologist J. W. Meigen in 1818.
About a third of the several hundred mold species in this genus have a sexual reproductive stage, and some cause infections while others hold commercial value — which genus?
Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Ranging from 1 to 5 meters tall and found across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, this shrub genus's best-known species is the European type also called barberry — what genus is it?
Berberis is a large genus of deciduous and evergreen shrubs from 1-5 m (3+12-16+12 ft) tall, found throughout temperate and subtropical regions of the world (apart from Australia).
This branch of biology studies how plants have grown, reproduced, and evolved over the last 3.5 billion years of life on Earth — what field is it?
Botany is the branch of natural science and biology that studies the growth, reproduction and evolution of plants over the last 3.5 billion years of life on earth.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.

Appearing in early childhood with symptoms like poor coordination and stiff or weak muscles, this group of movement disorders does not worsen over time even though symptoms become more noticeable in a child's first years — which condition?
Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).
Born in 1863, this Italian mathematician is remembered chiefly as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
Corrado Segre (20 August 1863 - 18 May 1924) was an Italian mathematician who is remembered today as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry.
Affecting some 280 million people worldwide, this state of low mood saps motivation and the pleasure once taken in activities — what is it?
Depression (mood) is a mental state of low mood and aversion to activity.
Sometimes triggered by lead poisoning or reactions to neuroleptic drugs, this neurological disorder produces involuntary, twisting muscle contractions — what is it?

Dystonia is a neurological hyperkinetic movement disorder in which sustained or repetitive muscle contractions occur involuntarily, resulting in twisting and repetitive movements or abnormal fixed postures.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?
The excessive buildup of collagen-rich connective tissue after chronic inflammation or repeated injury, leaving a permanent scar that can choke off organ function — what's this process called?
Fibrosis is the development of fibrous connective tissue in response to an injury.
Sometimes mistakenly called the 'stomach flu' even though it's unrelated to influenza, this inflammation of the gut is usually viral, with rotavirus the top cause in children. What condition is it?
Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract including the stomach and intestine.
The first of America's Teen Series fighters, this twin-tail jet with swing wings debuted at sea on the USS Enterprise in 1974. What is it?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the giant crab spider or cane spider, this member of the huntsman spider family is native to the tropics but has spread into subtropical areas — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria is a species of spider in the family Sparassidae, the huntsman spiders.
About the size of an almond in humans, this small brain region links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland — what is it?
Hypothalamus (pl.: hypothalami; from Ancient Greek (hup) 'under' and (thlamos) 'chamber') is a small part of the vertebrate brain that contains a number of nuclei with a variety of functions.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it kills with a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell — or punch straight through a mammal's skull between the ears. Which spotted predator is it?
Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.
This Indian aerospace engineer served as secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of both ISRO and the Space Commission — who is he?
K. Sivan (born 14 April 1957) is an Indian aerospace engineer who served as the secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of ISRO and Space Commission.

Seen using a silver stain and grown on media containing the amino acid cysteine, this genus of bacteria causes a severe pneumonia-like illness as well as a milder flu-like illness called Pontiac fever — name the genus?
Legionella is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria that can be seen using a silver stain or grown in a special media that contains cysteine, an amino acid.

Fatigue, memory problems, breathlessness, and sleep trouble that the WHO marks as setting in three months after infection — symptoms that vanish and reappear for weeks or years. What condition is this?
Long COVID is a group of health problems persisting or developing after an initial period of COVID19 from 2 infection.
An autosomal dominant flaw in the fibrillin-making FBN1 gene gives this disorder its tell-tale look — tall, long-limbed, double-jointed — while quietly threatening the aorta — what is it?
Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multi-systemic genetic disorder that affects the connective tissue.
This British-Lebanese geometer co-founded topological K-theory and lent his name to a famous index theorem — and won both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize. Who was he?
Michael Atiyah (22 April 1929 - 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.

Though its 83 species can grow as tall as trees, this genus is technically herbaceous, its 'trunk' just tightly wrapped leaf stalks, and it gives us edible bananas, plantains, and fiber for cloth — what genus is it?
Musa (plant) is one of three genera in the family Musaceae.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandin production, though it carries a risk of liver side effects. Name the drug?
Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this condition wears down joint cartilage over years, often first striking the knuckles nearest your fingertips and the base of the thumb — what is it?
Osteoarthritis is a type of degenerative joint disease that results from breakdown of joint cartilage and underlying bone.

Also known as underage medicine, this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — typically up to age 18 in most of the Commonwealth, but only 12 in India. Name the medical specialty?

Pediatrics (American English), also spelled paediatrics (British English) and also known as underage medicine, is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, toddlers, children, adolescents, and young adults.
When this domesticated mammal reached Europe from the Near East, it interbred so freely with local wild boar that scholars still argue whether it's a distinct species — what animal is it?
Pig (Sus domesticus), also called swine (pl.: swine) or hog, is an omnivorous, domesticated, even-toed, hoofed mammal.

Caused by the loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15, this rare genetic disorder leads to weak muscles and poor feeding in infancy, then constant hunger and risk of obesity in childhood — what's it called?

Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by a loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15. A similar mechanism occurs in Angelman syndrome, except the defective chromosome 15 is from the mother, or two copies are from the father.
This white, odorless nitroamine explosive, widely used since World War II, is the explosive agent inside C-4 plastic explosive — what is it called?
RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Made by steaming dehusked oat groats before flattening them under heavy rollers and lightly toasting them, this whole-grain food becomes porridge when cooked — which product?
Rolled oats are a type of lightly processed whole-grain food.
Caused by a lack of vitamin C, this deficiency disease shows up after about a month of poor diet with weakness, sore limbs, gum disease, and bleeding from the skin — what is it?
Scurvy is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
Unlike its shelled cousin the snail, this soft-bodied land mollusk gets by with no shell at all, or at most a tiny internal remnant of one — what animal is it?
Slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
This Taiwanese-American software engineer co-founded and served as CTO of a massively popular video-sharing platform before later building MixBit through his company AVOS Systems — who is he?
Steve Chen (Wade-; born August 25, 1978) is a Taiwanese-American software engineer and Internet entrepreneur who is a co-founder and ex-CTO of YouTube.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
What's the name for hardened, foul-smelling deposits of trapped debris that form in the crevices of the tonsils, sometimes visible as white flecks at the back of the throat?
Tonsil stones are mineralizations of debris within the crevices of the tonsils.
Occasionally causing hearing loss or bone marrow suppression as side effects, this IV antibiotic treats MRSA infections and, in oral form, a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic medication used to treat certain bacterial infections.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Found naturally in coffee, bread and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is produced when your liver partly oxidizes ethanol — making it a chief culprit behind the hangover. What is it?

Born as a Spanish CASA design and now built by a major European aerospace conglomerate, this twin-engine turboprop transport plane first flew in November 1997 and entered Spanish Air Force service in 1999 — which aircraft?
Airbus C295: European tactical military transport aircraft.
Nicknamed the death cap, this deadly poisonous fungus resembles edible species like Caesar's mushroom and is native to Europe — what is it?
Amanita phalloides: Poisonous mushroom (death cap). The large fruiting bodies appear in summer and autumn; the caps are generally greenish in colour with a white stipe and gills.
Native to the eastern Mediterranean, this flowering herb's seeds taste similar to fennel, licorice, and tarragon and flavor candies and spirits — what is it?
Also called gobō, this Eurasian plant is cultivated in Japan for its edible root but has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils elsewhere — which species?
Arctium lappa: Species of flowering plant. It has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils in North America, Australia, and other regions, but is cultivated for its vegetable root.
An aurora glows when charged particles from the Sun collide with which two gases high in Earth's atmosphere?
The collisions excite oxygen and nitrogen atoms, which release the energy as light -- oxygen gives the familiar green and red, nitrogen the blues and purples.

This relationship, expressed as A = εcl, links how much light a solution absorbs directly to its concentration — what is this principle called, named after two scientists whose work dates back to the mid-18th century?
Beer–Lambert law: Scientific law describing absorption of light.
This small Old World flycatcher breeds in rocky habitats from the British Isles to Morocco and central China, staying put in milder areas but migrating from colder ones — what bird is it?
Black redstart: Species of bird. The black redstart (Phoenicurus ochruros) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family.
Formed from the C5-T1 spinal nerve roots, this network of nerves runs through the neck and over the first rib to supply the shoulder, arm, and hand — what is it?
Brachial plexus: Network of nerves. This plexus extends from the spinal cord, through the cervicoaxillary canal in the neck, over the first rib, and into the armpit.
Caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, this disease triggered a global health emergency declared by the WHO in March 2020 and lifted in May 2023 — which disease?
COVID-19: Contagious disease caused by SARS-CoV-2. Starting in January 2020, the disease spread worldwide, resulting in the COVID-19 pandemic.
Derived from Greek words for 'heart' and 'study,' this branch of internal medicine covers coronary artery disease, heart failure, and electrophysiology — which medical field?
Cardiology: Branch of medicine dealing with the heart.
Triggered by anything from a stroke to a bout of altitude sickness, this dangerous buildup of fluid inside the skull raises pressure on brain tissue and can cause seizures or worse — what is it?
Cerebral edema: Excess accumulation of fluid in the brain.

An essential nutrient your liver can only partly produce on its own, this compound builds phospholipids in cell membranes and helps make a neurotransmitter for muscle control, and occurs naturally in eggs, meat, and fish — which nutrient?
Choline: Chemical compound and essential nutrient. Choline is a cation with the chemical formula [(CH3)3NCH2CH2OH]+.

This ancient insect order traces back to the Late Jurassic, with chewing-mouthpart ancestors called "roachoids" scuttling around some 320 million years ago — yet only about 30 of its 4,600 species ever moved in with us. Which creature is it?
Cockroach: Insects of the order Blattodea.

Used in Chinese medicine for over 1,500 years, this genus of parasitic fungi infects insects and other arthropods, taking its name from Greek and Latin words meaning 'club' and 'head' — which genus is it?
Cordyceps: Genus of fungi. Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.
Sometimes called 'bipolar III,' this mood disorder involves cycling periods of mild depression and elevated mood that never reach the severity of full manic or depressive episodes — what is it?
Cyclothymia: Mental disorder. Cyclothymia differs from bipolar disorder in the fact that major depression and mania are not found.
Whether for an object, a process, or a system, this is the intentional concept or proposal created by a thinking agent, balancing purpose, aesthetics, and constraints — what single word names it?
Design: Plan for the construction of an object or system.
Brought to Australia as an infant, this geologist joined Shackleton's Nimrod Expedition and became a leading figure of the Heroic Age of Antarctic exploration — who is it?
Douglas Mawson: Australian geologist and explorer of the Antarctic (1882–1958)
This membrane-bound series of protein complexes shuttles electrons through redox reactions, building a proton gradient that ultimately powers the synthesis of ATP — what's it called?
Electron transport chain: Energy-producing metabolic pathway.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.

This branch of Islamic scholarship interprets the Quran and sunnah through jurist reasoning, producing fatwas — while sharia itself is seen as unchanging, this human field is considered fallible. What is it called?
Fiqh: Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, whereas sharia is considered immutable and infallible by Muslims, fiqh is considered fallible and changeable.
This cold-weather injury turns skin white or waxy-blue after tissue actually freezes, often preceded by a tingling, numb warning stage called frostnip — what is it?
Frostbite: Effect of low temperature on skin and other tissues.

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
Born from an accidental 18th-century cross between the sweet orange and the pomelo in Barbados, this citrus hybrid is nicknamed the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit: Citrus fruit. The grapefruit (Citrus × paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

Marketed under a well-known brand name, this typical antipsychotic treats everything from schizophrenia to Tourette tics, but carries risks of tardive dyskinesia and dangerous QT-interval prolongation — what drug is it?
Haloperidol: Typical antipsychotic medication. Haloperidol, sold under the brand name Haldol among others, is a typical antipsychotic medication.
Named after the 19th-century physicist who proved electromagnetic waves exist, which SI unit measures one cycle per second?
Hertz: SI unit of frequency. The hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.
This condition involves a buildup of cerebrospinal fluid around the brain, causing headaches, vision problems, and in babies a rapidly enlarging head — what is it?
Hydrocephalus: Abnormal increase in cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.
Making up roughly 75% of antibodies found in the human bloodstream, which antibody type is produced by plasma B cells and features two paratopes?
A Harvard chemistry professor who studied chlorophyll and helped develop poison gas in WWI, he later became Harvard's president and the first U.S. ambassador to West Germany — who is he?
Nicknamed "Marvellous Merchiston," this 16th-century Scottish laird discovered logarithms and popularized the decimal point — who was this mathematical wizard?
Deafened by childhood illness and rerouted from competitive diving, she became a Hollywood stunt pioneer and earned the title 'the fastest woman in the world.' Who was she?
Kitty O'Neil: American stuntwoman and racer (1946–2018)
Named after the Latin for 'ghosts of the dead' for their large eyes and nocturnal habits, these primates are found only on Madagascar — what are they?
Lemur: Clade of primates endemic to the island of Madagascar.

Providing the USAF with intercontinental strategic airlift for oversized cargo, this jumbo transport is among the largest military aircraft ever built and shares lineage with the smaller Starlifter — what is it?
Lockheed C-5 Galaxy: American heavy military transport aircraft.

With a fruiting body resembling an open umbrella, this fungus often grows in fairy rings across Eurasian pastures and is prized as a good edible despite resembling toxic look-alikes — what's its scientific name?
Macrolepiota procera: Species of fungus. Macrolepiota procera, the parasol mushroom, is a basidiomycete fungus with a large, prominent fruiting body resembling a parasol.
In 2014 this Stanford mathematician became the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal, honored for her work on the geometry of Riemann surfaces — who was she?
Patented in 1922 and later marketed as Novalgin or Analgin, this painkiller's sale is restricted in some countries due to a rare blood-cell risk called agranulocytosis — what is it?
Metamizole: Medication. Metamizole or dipyrone is a painkiller, spasm reliever, and fever reliever drug.
Marketed under names like Rogaine and Loniten, this medication treats high blood pressure but is best known over-the-counter for combating hair loss — what's the drug?
Minoxidil: Medication to treat high blood pressure and alopecia.
This contagious, vaccine-preventable viral disease is best known for causing painful swelling of the glands beside the jaw — its hallmark symptom. What is it?
Mumps: Human disease caused by paramyxovirus.
Discovered in 1885 by Carl Auer von Welsbach, this rare-earth element tarnishes quickly in air and produces pink, purple, and yellow compounds when oxidized — which element, atomic number 60?
Neodymium: Chemical element with atomic number 60 (Nd)

A French apothecary and physician who studied at Avignon until the plague closed it, he's far better remembered for 942 cryptic quatrains said to foretell the future — by what Latinised name is he known?
Nostradamus: French apothecary, astrologer and seer (1503–1566)
Common in adolescents during growth spurts, this condition causes a painful bump just below the knee from inflammation where the patellar ligament attaches to the shinbone — what is it?

Osgood–Schlatter disease: Inflammation of the patellar ligament. Osgood–Schlatter disease (OSD) is inflammation of the patellar ligament at the tibial tuberosity (apophysitis) usually affecting adolescents during growth spurts.

Native across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this medium-sized game bird's family ties are murkier than expected — genetically, some species lean toward pheasants, others toward junglefowl. What bird is it?
Partridge: Common name for a type of bird.
Synthesized in 1938 by German chemist Otto Eisleb and later marketed as Demerol, this synthetic opioid was the go-to pain medication for much of the 20th century — what is it?
Pethidine: Opioid analgesic. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.

Not approved for general use in the US but sold across Europe for conditions such as vertigo and cortical myoclonus, this drug is a cyclic derivative of the neurotransmitter GABA and belongs to the 'racetam' group — what is it?
Domesticated some 7,000 to 10,000 years ago in what is now southern Peru, this starchy underground tuber belongs to the nightshade family — what is it?
Potato: Starchy tuber used as a staple food.
This Greco-Roman scholar authored the Almagest on astronomy and the Geography, a treatise on maps and geographic knowledge — who is he?

In this condition, tiny arteries spasm and starve the fingers of blood, classically turning them white, then blue, then a burning red as flow returns. It's named for the physician who first described it in 1862 — what is it?
Raynaud syndrome: Medical condition in which spasm of arteries causes episodes of reduced blood flow.
Winner of the 1905 Nobel Prize for his tuberculosis research, this German physician's 1876 discovery of the anthrax bacterium is considered the birth of modern bacteriology — who is he?
Robert Koch: German physician and bacteriologist (1843–1910)
Held together by electrostatic forces called ionic bonds, this type of chemical compound pairs positive and negative ions into a substance with zero net charge — what class of compound?
Salt (chemistry): Chemical compound involving ionic bonding.

Discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius and named after the moon because of its resemblance to an element named for the Earth, this semiconductor finds use in glassmaking, pigments, and photocells — what element is it?
Selenium: Chemical element with atomic number 34 (Se)
Housing the eyes, ears, nose, and brain, this bony structure at the head end of a vertebrate is built from cranial bones, facial bones, and tiny fused ossicles — what is it?
Skull: Bony structure that forms the head in vertebrates.
Sold under the brand name Aldactone, this diuretic medication treats heart failure and acne, and is also used to block testosterone's effects during feminizing hormone therapy — what is it?
NATO nicknamed this Soviet variable-sweep-wing tactical bomber 'Fencer'; it was the USSR's first plane with an integrated digital navigation-and-attack system — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-24: Family of Soviet strike aircraft.
The lone living family within its primate infraorder, these small Southeast Asian mammals favor forests thick with liana vines, which give them vertical support as they climb — which animal?
The body's primary muscle of respiration, this dome-shaped sheet separates the chest cavity from the abdomen and contracts to pull air into the lungs — what is it?
Thoracic diaphragm: Sheet of internal skeletal muscle.
Approved in the US in 1981, this sedating antidepressant from the SARI class racked up more than 24 million prescriptions in 2023, making it the fifth most common antidepressant — what is it?
Trazodone: Antidepressant medication. Trazodone is an antidepressant medication used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and insomnia.
This medical condition occurs when kidney failure allows urea and other metabolic waste products to build up dangerously in the bloodstream. What's it called?
Uremia: Excess urea in the blood due to kidney dysfunction.
Named for the French word for 'watcher,' this paraphilia involves secretly observing strangers in private, intimate moments and gave rise to the nickname 'Peeping Tom' — what is it called?
Voyeurism: Sexual interest in or practice of spying on people engaged in intimate behaviors.

When skin's protective barrier is broken, the body marches through a predictable sequence — hemostasis, inflammation, cell proliferation, and remodeling — to replace what was destroyed; what do we call this whole orchestrated repair process?
Wound healing: Series of events that restore integrity to damaged tissue after an injury.
Nobelium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for nobelium is No. Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
Nitrogen is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for nitrogen is N. Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.

Sebastian Maniscalco is a comedian. Sebastian Maniscalco (Italian: [maniˈskalko]; born July 8, 1973) is an American stand-up comedian and actor.
In what year was Rachel Weisz born?
Rachel Weisz: Rachel Hannah Weisz (born 7 March 1970) is a British actress.
In what year was Sarah Jessica Parker born?
Sarah Jessica Parker (born March 25, 1965) is an American actress and television producer.
In what year was Rachel McAdams born?
Rachel McAdams: Rachel Anne McAdams (born November 17, 1978) is a Canadian actress.
In what year was Natasha Richardson born?
Natasha Richardson: Natasha Jane Richardson (11 May 1963 – 18 March 2009) was an English actress.

Hrithik Roshan: Roshan has frequently collaborated with his father, Rakesh Roshan.
In what year was Paul Rudd born?
Paul Rudd: Paul Stephen Rudd (born April 6, 1969) is an American actor.
In what year was Idris Elba born?
Idris Elba: Sir Idrissa Akuna Elba ( IH-driss; born 6 September 1972) is an English actor, DJ, rapper, and producer.
In what year was Jodie Foster born?
Jodie Foster: Alicia Christian "Jodie" Foster (born November 19, 1962) is an American actress and filmmaker.
In what year was Gillian Anderson born?
Gillian Anderson: Gillian Leigh Anderson ( JIL-ee-ən; born August 9, 1968) is an American actress.
In what year was Ana de Armas born?
Ana de Armas: After moving to Los Angeles, de Armas had English-speaking roles in the psychological thriller Knock Knock (2015) and the comedy-crime film War Dogs (2016).
In what year did Bill Paxton die?
Bill Paxton: William Paxton (May 17, 1955 – February 25, 2017) was an American actor, filmmaker and musician.
In what year did John Wayne die?
John Wayne: Marion Robert Morrison (May 26, 1907 – June 11, 1979), known professionally as John Wayne, was an American actor.
In what year was Home Alone first released?
Home Alone is a 1990 American Christmas comedy film directed by Chris Columbus and written and produced by John Hughes.
In what year was Reptile first released?
Reptile (film): The film stars del Toro in the lead role, alongside Justin Timberlake, Alicia Silverstone, Eric Bogosian, Ato Essandoh, Domenick Lombardozzi, and Michael Pitt.
In what year was Nyad first released?
